description: Realistic 5G remote-driving latency (one-way). Models the latency distribution directly: a continuous right-skewed (lognormal) baseline -- the normal 5G delay variability -- plus brief Poisson handover/congestion spikes, per channel. Calibrated to representative published 5G teleoperation figures, NOT measured. Generated distribution: command/uplink median 35 ms, p95 87 ms, p99 231 ms, spikes to ~330 ms; camera/downlink glass-to-glass median 101 ms, p95 268 ms, p99 434 ms, spikes to ~570 ms. This replaces the earlier traffic-driven profiles, whose N-HiTS source (scm_youtube_ul_smoke) was a sparse 25 s smoke trace (97% zero) that degenerated to a constant baseline with rare max-pinned spikes. Drivable: no sustained outage. control=uplink command, camera=downlink video, manual mirrors control. Verify/regenerate the histogram via the snippet in the commit message or config/latency_profiles/5g_realistic_hist.png.
